- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.11) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+1.5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce early downward slope.
- If sentiment is consistently neutral or mildly positive, model underestimates downward momentum; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for downward correction.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); smooth out early forecast spikes with 1–2 day lagged smoothing.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize the reversal; delay downward correction by 1–2 days or reduce magnitude of drop.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion speed; reduce forecast slope toward true mean by 10–20% in later days.
